items.headline: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold ALB Stock After a 29% Dip in 6 Months?
items.snippet: Albemarle Corporation's ALB shares have tumbled 29.1% in the past six months, underperforming the Zacks Chemical - Diversified industry decline of 7.8% and the S&P 500's 13.9% increase. A pullback in lithium prices has weighed on ALB stock.

items.headline: Albemarle's Next CEO Inherits A $250 Million Swing Per Dollar
items.snippet: China's Supply Chokehold and the Pricing Hangover. JPMorgan analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas recently cut Albemarle's 2026 adjusted EBITDA estimate by 14.4% to $2.88 billion. Chinese prices averaged about $21,625 a ton so far in the third quarter, down from $24,810 in the second.

items.headline: Market Chatter: Lithium Miners' Profits Surge as Battery Storage Demand Drives Prices Higher
items.snippet: Lithium producers from China to Australia has seen profits soar as unrelenting demand from the energy storage sector pushes prices higher. US-headquartered Albemarle (ALB) noted that global lithium demand grew 45% through May this year, significantly outstripping supply.

items.headline: Albemarle's Lithium Math Turns Brutal
items.snippet: JPMorgan now expects lithium prices to remain in the low-$20-per-kilogram range. Third-quarter adjusted EBITDA expected at $668 million, down from $858 million in the second quarter. ALB Price Action: Albemarle shares were down 5.16% at $134.21 at the time of publication.

items.headline: Albemarle (ALB) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
items.snippet: Lithium demand is up 45% through May, primarily driven by continued strength in stationary storage. We now expect stationary storage battery production of 900 to 1,100 gigawatt hours in 2026, up 11% from our prior forecast.
